audit.whatIsWrong: Sylas is given five of seven stages in a matchup Sejuani wins 51.74% over 344 games, and the prose calls levels 3-5 a cooldown chess match rather than a losing phase.
audit.why: The chart and the whys disagree; the packet stage read matches the prose.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Sylas / Skill / Skill / Skill / Sejuani / Skill / Skill in both layers.

audit.whatIsWrong: Every spike referenced 'his E' and 'his R' with no numbers.
audit.why: Abscond/Abduct is 13/12/11/10/9s and only 400 range; Hijack is 80/55/30s, so by three points it is up almost every fight. Chain Lash is 10s at rank 1.
audit.corrected: Abscond's 13s at rank 1 and 400 range written into the phases, whys[3] and wants; Hijack's 30s at rank 3 written into the two-item phase.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two fields say Sylas can dash through or blink out of your Permafrost stun.
audit.why: A landed stun prevents ability casts, so Abscond cannot be used out of Permafrost. The real risk is the opposite ordering: he dashes during your Winter's Wrath arcs, before Frost caps and the stun exists. Written the wrong way round, the advice tells the player their stun is worthless when it is actually the answer.
audit.corrected: Restated: a landed Permafrost stops Abscond outright; the window he escapes through is the W arcs before Frost caps.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four fields call Sejuani's passive 'Permafrost armor' and say it drops the moment Chain Lash connects.
audit.why: The passive is Fury of the North and Riot's text says Frost Armor 'persists for a short time after Sejuani takes damage'. Permafrost is the E stun.
audit.corrected: Named Fury of the North / Frost Armor and its persistence stated.

audit.why: Kingslayer heals him on every lunge into a champion and scales with his AP item; without Grievous Wounds the extended trade never converts.

edits.after: At Level 1 Sylas's Chain Lash poke is close to free because it chips Frost Armor, though Fury of the North does linger briefly after damage — take W first, slap the wave, and give him nothing to trade against. Respect his double-Q range: if he clips you with the chain detonation he is already topping himself off, so stay outside that arc and let him push. At Level 3 your full sequence arrives — Q knock-up into double-W (both strikes build Frost) into E Permafrost stun is a real punish, and a landed stun stops Abscond outright, so the only thing that beats it is him dashing out during the W arcs before Frost caps.
edits.before: At Level 1 Sylas's Q Chain Lash poke is free damage because your passive Permafrost armor drops the moment he hits you twice — take W first, slap the wave, and give him nothing to trade against. The one thing you must respect is his double-Q range: if he clips you with the chain detonation he is already topping himself off with the passive heal, so stay just outside that arc and let him push. At Level 3 your full sequence arrives — Q knock-up into double-W (both strikes build Frost) into E Permafrost stun is a real punish, but only commit it when his E dash is visibly on cooldown or you will watch him blink through the stun and counter-drain you.

edits.after: Late game this matchup is about one critical threat: Hijack steals your Glacial Prison and throws it back with identical range and CC, and at rank 3 it is up every 30 seconds. Never face-check a side-lane Sylas with your R available if your team needs the next engage — spend it before he can copy it. Bring Grievous Wounds too, because Kingslayer heals him off every lunge and an un-shredded Sylas outlasts your chain. In teamfights you stay the superior initiator, but the lane is even and whoever lands CC first wins.
edits.before: Late game this matchup is about one critical threat: Sylas's R steals your Glacial Prison and throws it back with identical range and CC. Never face-check into a side-lane Sylas with your R available if your team needs you to initiate the next fight — save the ult for the actual engage and burn it before he can copy it. In teamfights you remain the superior initiator because your full Q-W-E Permafrost chain plus R is more CC than he can replicate with stolen tools, but the lane is genuinely even and the game is decided by who lands their CC chain first on the other.

notes: The load-bearing error: two fields told the player Sylas dashes out of Permafrost. A landed stun prevents ability casts, so Abscond cannot escape it — the escape window is the Winter's Wrath arcs before Frost caps, which is the opposite instruction. Also fixed the recurring 'passive Permafrost armor' naming (the passive is Fury of the North; Permafrost is the E stun) and the claim that it drops on contact when Riot's text says it persists a short time after damage. Added real numbers: Abscond 13s and 400 range, Hijack 30s at rank 3, plus Grievous Wounds against Kingslayer.
